notes: Portal fixes from the Tatcha go-live: kit names, a way back after ordering, as-is print cards that wait for their artwork · Disconnect a client from the ordering platform

entries.title: Portal fixes from the Tatcha go-live: kit names, a way back after ordering, as-is print cards that wait for their artwork
items: Kit and sub-category blocks: long names sit on the left and wrap to two lines instead of being centred and cut off at both ends.
After placing an order: View order, Keep shopping and Back to home. Refreshing the page still says the order was placed, with the same ways back into the portal.
A cart of only e-downloads can be placed — it no longer waits for a ship-to address it doesn't need.

As-is print cards: buyers are no longer asked to “add your details” to a card that has none. When the card's own artwork can't print yet, the buyer is told the warehouse is on it, and the moment the artwork is fixed or accepted with Print anyway, every order waiting for it goes ahead by itself. A waiting print job also has Try again with the SKU's artwork.
Print anyway now carries through to the print-ready copy of the file, so an accepted file actually reaches production.

entries.title: Disconnect a client from the ordering platform
items: Customer → Ordering platform → Connection → Disconnect…: unlink a client from the ordering platform once it's set up — for a brand that has left, or one linked to the wrong company. The card lists what will happen first: the link and the client's own credential go, orders stop coming in, nothing more is sent, and anything still waiting to go out is cancelled. SKUs, stock, orders and people stay.
Which SKU is which ordering platform part is kept so a reconnect picks up without importing again — or tick Also forget to clear it. Connecting again starts at Not live yet, so nothing old is sent.

entries.title: Pace: Staging and Live connected side by side, each customer's Pace ID checked against both; sign-in photos can show the whole image
items: Settings → Integrations → Pace: connect Pace Staging and Pace Live side by side — each with its own address, username and password (stored encrypted) and its own Connect & check. Nothing is written to Pace yet; monthly billing jobs come next and will run against whichever one you pick.

Sign-in page photo fit (Design studio → Sign-in): Fill, as before, or Show whole image — the whole picture with nothing cropped, the page colour around it. For logos and artwork that mustn't be cut off.
Customer → Billing → Pace: the customer's Pace customer ID. Saving checks it in every connected Pace and shows the customer's name there, or says it isn't found, so a typo shows straight away.

entries.title: Ten home layouts, Order again and Reorder now, ten sign-in layouts with the form placed anywhere; Check now says when it couldn't check; signing in as someone is exactly their view
items: Ten home layouts for client portals (Design studio → Look → Home layout): Magazine, Bento, Lookbook, Shelf, Dashboard, Sticker book, Pastel counter, Routine, Vanity mirror and Love letter — each a different structure in the brand's own colours and fonts, with the real catalog and each buyer's usual items, orders and budget. A Style strength dial (Classic, Playful, Full) sets how much decoration they draw; Classic is the calm default. Standard stays as it was.

Order again on every past order — My orders, the home page's recent orders and the order page — and Reorder now on the order page, which places the same order again in one step (same items, address, shipping). Both follow today's rules: anything out of stock without backorders, no longer on offer or over a limit is left out of Order again with the reason, and Reorder now refuses rather than place part of an order; approvals apply as usual.

Settings → General → Updates → Check now used to show the last answer it had (and “You're on the latest version”) when it couldn't reach the version file. Now it says it couldn't check and why — no answer from GitHub, or what came back — with when the last good check was and how to update on the host instead.

Signing in as a portal user is now exactly their view in every case: someone waiting for a user group sees the waiting page, and a developer login lands on the API docs, for staff signed in as them too.

The portal sign-in page has ten layouts instead of three — Big photo, Photo on top, Brand colour, Frosted panel, Framed photo, Big type and On a slant join the three — and the form can sit left, centre or right, and top, middle or bottom; the logo, name and tagline can be left, centred or right too (Design studio → Sign-in).

entries.title: Stripe for card payments, artwork as a print product's picture, Security settings save with a button
items: Card payments can run on Stripe: under Settings → Integrations → Card payments choose Authorize.net or Stripe. Stripe's own secure card field at checkout; holds, captures and refunds as before; test keys for trying it out.

A print-on-demand product with no photo now shows page 1 of the customer's artwork in the portal — on its card in the shop and on its page — instead of a printer icon. Add photos and they take its place.

Settings → Security: the typed values (session limits, password length, audit forwarding) now save with a clear Save button — an Unsaved changes bar appears as soon as you change one, and Enter saves too.

entries.title: E-download SKUs, Developer logins, Print anyway, Remove file
items: E-download SKUs: a product whose stock is a file (PDF, Office, ZIP, image). Ordered like any product; once the order is live the buyer is emailed the file — attached up to 10 MB, and a Download button on the order — nothing is picked or shipped, and an order of only downloads closes at once (in a mixed order the boxes alone decide). A cart of only downloads needs no address or carrier. Rate cards get an E-download fee, per download, 0 = free.

A print file with images at 150–249 dpi (against a 300 dpi spec) shows “Prints softer than the spec” with Print anyway for managers, owners and admins — accepted, it goes to production, with who and when on the file and in the audit trail. 250–299 dpi is only a note; under 150 still needs a sharper file.
The same picture drawn several times in a PDF is listed once (“— used 9 times”), not nine times.

In a brand that uses user groups, a buyer with no group sees only the welcome page until someone places them — the same as a single sign-on arrival without one. Brand admins, approvers and API accounts are unchanged; brands with no groups stay open.
Print setup: Remove file takes the customer's PDF off a print SKU (the original stays in its history; print jobs already made keep it).

Brand guidelines: a page of don'ts (wrong colours, logo misuse) no longer feeds the suggested colours — its rules are still read — and the colours under a “Primary colours” heading lead, the first one becoming the primary.

Developer portal logins: someone building a brand's integration signs in to the API reference, the integration guide and a read-only list of the brand's keys — nothing to order or see. Only warehouse staff make them (Users → Role → Developer — API docs only); keys stay with you.

entries.title: Signed in without a user group: nothing to browse until someone places them
items: Someone who signs in through single sign-on without a user group no longer sees the brand's categories, search, cart, orders or reports — the menu is empty and every store page leads to one welcome page.
That page now speaks to the brand's own people: their access isn't set up yet, their portal administrator can add them (with the support email), or IT can add them to the portal group.
On the staff Users page, the group of someone waiting reads “No group — waiting” instead of “No group (open)”.

Single sign-on is in the audit trail properly: each sign-in names the person and the address it came from instead of “anonymous”, says what happened (created, updated, refused, which group), and opens to every value their identity provider sent.

Customer → Activity: each customer's own audit trail — sign-ins, single sign-on, their portal people, settings — with the same click-to-open detail. Reports → Audit trail rows open the same way and name portal people.

entries.title: Security: the API documentation viewer held back for an advisory
items: The interactive API reference stays on its previous version while its newest one carries a high-severity advisory in a file-matching library (GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf). Nothing changes on screen.

entries.title: The team hears when a new version is live
items: After Amphora updates, everyone on the staff side gets one email: “Version 1.76.0 is live”, with your logo and colours, a hello, and what changed since the version you came from — every release in between if a few were skipped.

It waits until the new version has been up for five minutes and is running well — the server answers, errors stay rare, nothing critical — so nobody is told about an update that's having trouble. Once per version; going back to an older version sends nothing.

Vendor logins, deactivated people and username + PIN accounts are left out; client portal users never get it. Owners and admins can turn it off, and send themselves a preview, under Settings → General → Updates. The wording can be changed under Settings → Email.
Single sign-on: Download our certificate — the signing certificate as a .cer file, for Okta’s Signature Certificate upload (portal Sign-in setup, the IT handout, and Settings → Single sign-on).

entries.title: Duplicate a SKU
items: Every SKU's page has Duplicate at the top right. It opens New SKU with everything filled in from that SKU — name, prices and price breaks, ordering rules, categories, kit contents, images, sizes, compliance and the brand's fields — so a new colour or size is a new code and a couple of changes.

The SKU code and the barcodes start empty, because they must be unique: the code box is ready to type in and reminds you it must differ. The copy starts with no stock or history; those stay with the original.

entries.title: Import SKU images in bulk
items: Import images, on a customer's SKUs tab, puts pictures on many SKUs at once: a sheet with two columns, sku and image (the file name), and a zip of the pictures — or the image files themselves.
Repeat a SKU on more rows to give it more pictures; the first row is its main one. Files are found by name, ignoring capitals and the folders in the zip.

Everything is checked before anything changes: unknown codes, files missing from the zip and non-pictures are listed by line, with Download rows to fix. New pictures go after a SKU's current ones, or tick Replace. Running the same import again adds nothing twice.

entries.title: Add many SKUs to a category from the Categories card
items: Open a category on the Categories card and its SKUs now show right under it, split In category and Not in category. Tick as many as you need — or the box at the top for every one shown — and Add to category puts them all in at once.
Search by code or name, see which other categories each SKU is already in, and take SKUs out the same way. No more opening each category's page to fill it.

entries.title: Find a kit part by code, name or UPC
items: On a kit's Kit contents tab, each part is now a search box instead of a long dropdown: type part of the SKU code, the product name or the UPC, and the matches list right under the row with their UPCs. Arrow keys move through them and Enter picks one; scanning a UPC picks that part straight away.
Every SKU of the brand can be found, not only the first 200 the old dropdown loaded. A part that's already in the kit is listed as “already in this kit” and can't be picked twice.
The SKU search behind the receiving and movement screens now matches barcodes too.

entries.title: Kit groups can limit how many the buyer picks
items: A group of Buyer's choice parts on a kit can now say how many of them the buyer takes: pick at least, pick at most. At least 1 and at most 1 on Hair Clips means the buyer gets one of the clips, never neither and never both, while each clip stays a Buyer's choice.

In the portal the group reads “Hair Clips — Pick 1”; choosing the other clip swaps the choice, a group that's full stops more picks, and Add to cart waits until every group has what it needs. Orders that break a group's limit are refused by name, wherever they come from (portal, API, import).
“Buyer picks up to” still caps the whole kit when it's set, and can be left blank when every Buyer's choice part is in a group with a limit.
The API takes kitGroupPicks on a SKU, and the Kit contents import has pick_at_least and pick_at_most columns.
